## Where does the axis start? {#baseline data-hold="true"}

```{=html}
<div class="bridgew" id="basew">
  <div class="sm-controls">
    <label class="sm-slider">Bar axis starts at <strong id="bs-label">0</strong>
      <input type="range" id="bs" min="0" max="10" step="0.5" value="0">
    </label>
  </div>
  <svg id="bs-plot" viewBox="0 0 1160 280" role="img" aria-label="Two bars, April and October 2004 mean benzene, with an axis whose starting value can be changed"></svg>
  <div class="sm-readout" id="bs-out" aria-live="polite"></div>
</div>
<script>
(function () {
  const root = document.getElementById('basew'); if (!root) return;
  root.addEventListener('click', (e) => e.stopPropagation());
  const A = 10.39, Bv = 13.53;   // mean benzene, April and October 2004 (Lab 04, Demo A)
  const W = 1160, H = 280, L = 64, R = 16, T = 20, B = 40, top = 15;
  function draw() {
    const b0 = +document.getElementById('bs').value;
    document.getElementById('bs-label').textContent = b0;
    const V = (v) => T + (1 - (v - b0) / (top - b0)) * (H - T - B);
    let g = '';
    for (let v = Math.ceil(b0); v <= top; v += (top - b0 > 8 ? 5 : 1)) g += `<line x1="${L}" x2="${W - R}" y1="${V(v)}" y2="${V(v)}" stroke="#B9C1C6"/><text x="${L - 10}" y="${V(v) + 6}" text-anchor="end" font-size="17" fill="#333F4A">${v}</text>`;
    g += `<line x1="${L}" x2="${L}" y1="${T}" y2="${H - B}" stroke="#333F4A" stroke-width="1.5"/><line x1="${L}" x2="${W - R}" y1="${H - B}" y2="${H - B}" stroke="#333F4A" stroke-width="1.5"/>`;
    [[A, 'April 2004', '#0F6E6B', 0.3], [Bv, 'October 2004', '#E29A2D', 0.7]].forEach(([v, lab, c, f]) => {
      const x = L + (W - L - R) * f;
      g += `<rect x="${x - 90}" y="${V(v)}" width="180" height="${H - B - V(v)}" fill="${c}"/><text x="${x}" y="${V(v) - 8}" text-anchor="middle" font-size="18" font-weight="700" fill="#1C242B">${v.toFixed(1)}</text><text x="${x}" y="${H - 12}" text-anchor="middle" font-size="17" fill="#333F4A">${lab}</text>`;
    });
    document.getElementById('bs-plot').innerHTML = g;
    const seen = (Bv - b0) / (A - b0), lie = (seen - 1) / (Bv / A - 1);
    document.getElementById('bs-out').innerHTML = `<span class="sm-chip">the second bar looks <b>${seen.toFixed(2)}×</b> as tall</span><span class="sm-chip seen">the data: <b>${(Bv / A).toFixed(2)}×</b></span><span class="sm-chip ${lie < 1.1 ? 'seen' : lie < 3 ? 'blurred' : 'missed'}">lie factor <b>${lie.toFixed(1)}</b></span>`;
  }
  document.getElementById('bs').addEventListener('input', draw);
  draw();
})();
</script>
```

::: {.note-line}
Lie factor (Tufte) = the change the reader sees ÷ the change in the data, each as a relative change: (seen ratio − 1) ÷ (data ratio − 1). An honest bar chart has 1.0.
:::

```{=html}
  const MON = ['Apr 04', 'May 04', 'Jun 04', 'Jul 04', 'Aug 04', 'Sep 04', 'Oct 04', 'Nov 04', 'Dec 04', 'Jan 05', 'Feb 05', 'Mar 05'];
  const LEN = [30, 31, 30, 31, 31, 30, 31, 30, 31, 31, 28, 31], START = LEN.map((_, k) => LEN.slice(0, k).reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0));
  const N = D.length, W = 1160, H = 280, L = 64, R = 16, T = 14, B = 40, top = 26;
  const X = (k) => L + (k / (N - 1)) * (W - L - R), V = (v) => T + (1 - v / top) * (H - T - B);
  function draw() {
    let f = +document.getElementById('wf').value, t = +document.getElementById('wt').value;
    if (t <= f) { t = f + 1; document.getElementById('wt').value = t; }
    document.getElementById('wf-label').textContent = MON[f]; document.getElementById('wt-label').textContent = MON[t];
    const k0 = START[f], k1 = START[t] + LEN[t] - 1, pts = [];
    for (let k = k0; k <= k1; k++) if (D[k] !== null) pts.push([k, D[k]]);
    const mx = pts.reduce((a, p) => a + p[0], 0) / pts.length, my = pts.reduce((a, p) => a + p[1], 0) / pts.length;
    let sxy = 0, sxx = 0; for (const [x, y] of pts) { sxy += (x - mx) * (y - my); sxx += (x - mx) ** 2; }
    const s = sxy / sxx, c = my - s * mx;
    let g = `<rect x="${X(k0)}" y="${T}" width="${X(k1) - X(k0)}" height="${H - T - B}" fill="#DFC98F" opacity=".45"/>`;
    for (const v of [0, 10, 20]) g += `<line x1="${L}" x2="${W - R}" y1="${V(v)}" y2="${V(v)}" stroke="#B9C1C6"/><text x="${L - 10}" y="${V(v) + 6}" text-anchor="end" font-size="17" fill="#333F4A">${v}</text>`;
    MON.forEach((m, k) => { g += `<text x="${X(START[k] + 15)}" y="${H - 12}" text-anchor="middle" font-size="15" fill="#333F4A">${m.slice(0, 3)}</text>`; });
    g += `<line x1="${L}" x2="${L}" y1="${T}" y2="${H - B}" stroke="#333F4A" stroke-width="1.5"/><line x1="${L}" x2="${W - R}" y1="${H - B}" y2="${H - B}" stroke="#333F4A" stroke-width="1.5"/>`;
    D.forEach((v, k) => { if (v !== null) g += `<circle cx="${X(k).toFixed(1)}" cy="${V(v).toFixed(1)}" r="2.6" fill="#0F6E6B" opacity=".75"/>`; });
    g += `<line x1="${X(k0)}" x2="${X(k1)}" y1="${V(c + s * k0)}" y2="${V(c + s * k1)}" stroke="#E29A2D" stroke-width="4"/>`;
    document.getElementById('wn-plot').innerHTML = g;
    const per30 = s * 30;
    document.getElementById('wn-out').innerHTML = `<span class="sm-chip ${per30 > 0.5 ? 'missed' : per30 < -0.5 ? 'blurred' : 'seen'}">${MON[f]} to ${MON[t]}: trend <b>${per30 >= 0 ? '+' : '−'}${Math.abs(per30).toFixed(2)} µg/m³ per 30 days</b></span><span class="sm-n">${pts.length} days</span>`;
  }
  ['wf', 'wt'].forEach((id) => document.getElementById(id).addEventListener('input', draw));
  draw();
})();
</script>
```

[Try August to October, then October to February. Same station, same year. Data: De Vito, UCI Air Quality, doi:10.24432/C59K5F, CC BY 4.0.]{.source}

## Activity 1 · The AI's bar chart {#act1 .activity}

[Pairs · 10 minutes · Lab 04, Step 4]{.act-label}

```{=html}
<pre class="code-slide"><span>monthly = df["C6H6_ugm3"].resample("MS").mean()</span><span>ax.bar(monthly.index.strftime("%b %Y"), monthly.values)</span><span>ax.set_ylim(int(0.9 * monthly.min()), monthly.max() * 1.05)   <b class="c"># zoom in on the difference</b></span><span>ax.set_title("Benzene was far worse in the second month")</span></pre>
```

::: {.prompt .small}
Every number on this chart is correct. Name two lines that make it mislead, and rewrite the title so it states only what the data show.
:::

::: {.selfstudy}
Studying alone: write your two lines and your title, then go on.
:::

## What to change {#act1-fix}

::: {.beforeafter}
::: {}
[Line 3: the axis]{.label}
The bars start just below the smaller mean, so the reader compares the leftover tips. For Demo A the second bar looks 3.3 times as tall; the data say 1.3. Use `ax.set_ylim(0, None)`, or points instead of bars.
:::
::: {}
[Line 4: the title]{.label}
"Far worse" is a judgement the figure was drawn to support. State the numbers: "Mean benzene: April 10.4, October 13.5 µg/m³ (+30 %); the middle half of the hours overlaps."
:::
:::

[The code did what it was asked. The request, "show the difference clearly", was the problem.]{.note-line}

## Rules for an honest figure {#rules}

::: {.checks4}
::: {.c4}
[Bars from zero]{.label}
A bar shows a value by its length. Points and lines may use a narrower axis; label it.
:::
::: {.c4}
[Show the spread]{.label}
A mean of 700 hours needs its range: the middle half, or the full distribution.
:::
::: {.c4}
[Say the window]{.label}
State the period and why it was chosen. Show the year if you claim a trend.
:::
::: {.c4}
[Title = finding]{.label}
The title states what the data show, with numbers, not what you hope the reader concludes.
:::
:::

[Ask the AI for the figure that answers a question, not for one that "shows the difference clearly".]{.note-line}
